leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County, Altitude Express, Inc. v. Zarda, R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes Inc. v. EEOC - U.S. Supreme Court
leads.documents: Establishes that workplace discrimination on basis of sexual orientation or gender identity is sex discrimination under Title VII, therefore protects LGBT employees in Wyoming despite no state statute.
leads.detail: Cited as June 15, 2020 ruling; no URL visible in provided text

leads.title: Guzzo v. Mead - U.S. District Court (Judge Scott Skavdahl)
leads.documents: Federal ruling striking down Wyoming's same-sex marriage ban, leading to legal same-sex marriage in Wyoming.
leads.detail: Ruled Oct 17, took effect Oct 21, 2014 when state officials notified court they would not appeal; Governor Matt Mead context cited

leads.title: Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals same-sex marriage rulings
leads.documents: Binding precedent on Wyoming courts that bans on same-sex marriage are unconstitutional, cited as reason marriage became legal.
leads.detail: Referenced via U.S. Supreme Court Oct 6, 2014 denial leaving precedent standing; no URL visible

leads.title: Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act (2009) - U.S. Congress
leads.documents: Federal expansion of hate crime definition to include sexual orientation and gender identity; key enforcement machinery given Wyoming has no state hate crime law.
leads.detail: Passed 2009; linked in text to 1998 murder of Matthew Shepard near Laramie, Wyoming; no URL visible

leads.title: Wyoming House Bill 72 - public restroom biological sex segregation (2025)
leads.documents: Transgender bathroom ban requiring all public restrooms be segregated by biological sex - direct trans-visitor safety/access issue.
leads.detail: Signed April 2025 by Gov. Mark Gordon, takes effect July 1, 2025; no URL visible

leads.title: Wyoming ban on sexual reassignment surgery and gender-affirming care on children (2024 Legislature)
leads.documents: Criminalizes/prohibits gender-affirming healthcare for minors - documents legal risk environment for trans youth and families.
leads.detail: Overwhelmingly passed both houses March 2024, signed by Gov. Mark Gordon, effective July 1; no URL visible

leads.title: Wyoming transgender athlete ban (2023 Legislature)
leads.documents: Legally bans transgender athletes from female sports and athletics teams.
leads.detail: Passed March 2023, Gov. Mark Gordon took no action (no veto/signature) so became law automatically, effective July 1, 2023; no URL visible

leads.title: Wyoming Vital Statistics Services and Department of Transportation gender marker policies
leads.documents: Documents state machinery for legal gender recognition: birth certificate requires sex reassignment surgery + court order + ID + doctor letter; driver's license/state ID requires Gender Designation Change Request Form signed by physician/therapist/counselor/social worker.
leads.detail: Described as agency requirements; form title quoted as 'Gender Designation Change Request Form'; no URL visible

leads.title: Wyoming SF 115 (2015) and city ordinances - Jackson, Casper, Laramie
leads.documents: Documents absence of statewide anti-discrimination statute covering sexual orientation/gender identity vs. local protections in employment, housing, public accommodations.
leads.detail: SF 115 approved Senate Judiciary 6-1 Feb 3, 2015, Senate 24-6 Feb 10, House committee 6-2 Feb 20, rejected House 26-33 Feb 24, 2015; Jackson/Casper/Laramie ordinances cover orientation and identity; Cheyenne/Gillette cover city employment orientation only; no URL visible

leads.title: Movement Advancement Project - Wyoming's Equality Profile / Equaldex - LGBT Rights in Wyoming
leads.documents: Institutional human-rights profiles summarizing Wyoming LGBTQ legal status and enforcement.
leads.detail: Listed in External links section as 'Wyoming's Equality Profile - via the Movement Advancement Project' and 'LGBT Rights in Wyoming - via Equaldex'; no URLs visible in provided text
